rules.statement: An ASP.NET Core host served by Kestrel must set `KestrelServerOptions.AddServerHeader` to `false` so that no response carries a `Server` header.
rules.why: Naming the server software helps an anonymous caller fingerprint the stack, and the OWASP HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet recommends that a response not name it.
rules.check: Look for a host's Kestrel setup or service registration that leaves `AddServerHeader` at its default of true, or a new host that doesn't register the shared server-header suppression.

rules.statement: Apply the Server header suppression in every environment, without making it conditional on `IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment()` or any other environment check.
rules.why: When the setting holds in every environment, Development responses match Production responses.
rules.check: Look for `AddServerHeader = false`, or the registration that sets it, wrapped in an environment condition.

rules.statement: Don't depend on an ingress or reverse proxy to strip the `Server` header. Suppress it in the host itself.
rules.why: A host reached directly, in development or behind another proxy, would still name itself.
rules.check: Look for changes that remove host-side suppression of the Server header, or that justify leaving it out because a proxy strips the header.

rules.statement: Set non-TLS Kestrel options such as `AddServerHeader` through a composable options action, such as `services.Configure<KestrelServerOptions>` in a shared registration method. Don't add them to the host's TLS-focused `ConfigureKestrel` call.
rules.why: Options actions compose, so every host can call one registration instead of repeating the setting. Keeping the setting out of `ConfigureKestrel` leaves that block about TLS only, because `ConfigureHttpsDefaults` keeps only its last action.
rules.check: Look for `AddServerHeader` or other unrelated Kestrel settings added inside a host's `ConfigureKestrel` or `ConfigureHttpsDefaults` block, or copied separately into each host.

rules.statement: In a test project, a host's integration tests assert that `KestrelServerOptions.AddServerHeader` is `false` on the built host.
rules.why: The ADR requires the integration test to check the option on the built host, so a regression that brings the header back is caught.
rules.check: Look for a host integration test project with no assertion that the resolved `KestrelServerOptions.AddServerHeader` is false, or a change that removes that assertion.
